title: Current Google Policy Re-Verification
methodology: Re-fetched Google's current AdSense/Publisher Policy documentation fresh for this certification rather than reusing AQ-06A's earlier fetch from the same day — AQ-05 established that documentation can and does change between certifications, and that discipline is applied here even though only hours separate AQ-06A and this re-check, not assumed unnecessary because of the short interval.
sources_checked: https://support.google.com/publisherpolicies/answer/10852414 (Publisher Standards change log — the authoritative record of what has actually changed and when)
https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/16737 (Invalid traffic policy — explicitly requested by this ticket, not checked in AQ-06A)

change_log_review.finding: Checked the Publisher Standards change log directly (the authoritative source for what changed and when, not inferred from re-reading policy prose). The 5 most recent entries: August 2025 (OFAC sanctions list update, Syria), July 2025 (dishonest declarations policy clarification, no enforcement change), March 2025 (online gambling restriction scope), February 2025 (two updates: disclosure-clause alignment with privacy policies, and privacy-enhancing-technology-related ad serving changes), January 2025 (Russia/Ukraine regional monetization consolidation).
change_log_review.relevance_to_pairingmethod: None of the 5 most recent changes touch content quality, low-value content, AI-generated content, ad placement, or invalid traffic — the categories most relevant to this site's situation. No policy shift has occurred since AQ-06A that would change any conclusion reached there.
change_log_review.conclusion: Unlike AQ-04->AQ-05 (where FAQ rich results and Sitelinks Search Box had genuinely changed), no equivalent shift is found here. This is stated as a checked, evidenced finding, not an assumption.

adsense_eligibility.note: High-quality, original content; ability to access HTML source; policy compliance. No new requirements found.

publisher_policies_prohibited_content.note: Illegal content, IP infringement, dangerous/derogatory content, animal cruelty, misrepresentation, harmful health claims, deceptive practices, sexually explicit content, child exploitation — all confirmed still current, none applicable to this site's content.

restricted_content.note: PairingMethod has no gambling, alcohol-sales, adult, or other restricted-category content requiring regional handling.

invalid_traffic.note: Publisher responsibility to prevent artificially inflated clicks/impressions (self-clicks, encouraged clicks, automated tools). Entirely a future-state, post-monetization concern — the site currently serves 0 ads, so there is no traffic to be invalid. Correctly not applicable at this stage, same framing as AQ-06's ad-related policy items.

ad_placement.note: Ads cannot overlay/obstruct navigation, cannot exceed publisher content, no ads on low-value/under-construction screens. Assessed prospectively in AQ-06R6 (ad placement readiness), since no ads exist yet.

deceptive_behavior.note: No phishing, get-rich-quick, coordinated inauthentic behavior, or misrepresentation found anywhere on the site.

navigation_and_ux.note: Not a distinct Google policy category on its own, but Google's inventory-value policy references 'low-value content' partly through a UX lens — covered there.

original_value_adding_content.note: Google's policy prohibits ads on 'content-replicating screens without original commentary' — this describes copying third-party content, not originally-authored-but-formulaic writing, the same distinction AQ-06A drew. AQ-07's remediation improves the site's standing on the adjacent Helpful Content originality dimension without changing this policy's own scope.

scraped_replicated_content.note: No content on this site is copied or scraped from another source — every entity is originally authored, catalog-governed content, verified across AQ-01 through AQ-07.

low_value_content.note: AQ-06's finding (templated, jargon-leaking prose in 4 domains) was the site's clearest proximity to this concern, correctly classified then as a Helpful Content quality concern rather than a 'low-value content' policy violation. Re-assessed after AQ-07 in AQ-06R2.

site_behavior.note: No popups, interstitials, auto-playing media, or other disruptive behavior found (confirmed in AQ-06D, re-confirmed here via spot-check).

classification.quality_concerns_detail: AQ06-HC-01 (now CLOSED per AQ-06R baseline comparison, subject to independent re-verification in AQ-06R2) — the only item that ever bordered on a policy-adjacent concern (originality/low-value content), and it was never classified as an actual violation, only a quality concern requiring disclosure.
classification.recommendations_detail: Name Google/AdSense specifically in cookies.html once ads go live (currently describes 'advertising networks' generically) — a disclosure-completeness recommendation, not a current violation, carried forward unchanged from AQ-06A.

overall_certification: PASS — 0 policy violations, 0 policy risks. No genuine policy concern was found and then incorrectly downgraded to a mere recommendation; the one quality concern remains correctly classified as a Helpful Content matter, not a policy matter, consistent with Rule 3's requirement not to conflate categories.
